messages:
Sasha: kicking off a Q3 planning thread for private deployments. We need a clear sequencing decision: ship a control-plane-first path for VPC customers, or invest up-front in full on-prem + air-gapped packaging. Customers are asking for both. I want a recommended path + launch criteria that we can commit to for a 12-week horizon.
Jun: +1. Please add rough eng estimates and blockers so PM/Eng can align.
Taylor: Eng summary: control-plane-lite (customer VPC control plane, tenant isolation, SSO, basic KMS hooks) looks like ~6 weeks for core work + 2 weeks for hardening. Full on-prem packaging (installer, dependency bundles, validation matrix) is ~10-14 weeks. Air-gap adds offline model distribution, signature verification, and extra QA (~4 weeks).
Lina: Security/regulatory callouts: air-gapped installs require an audited offline import process, signed model artifacts, and documented key import flow (HSM/PKCS11). We also need operator RBAC and immutable audit logs for some finance customers — these are non-negotiable for those deals.
Omar: Sales input: two enterprise accounts are waiting on VPC control plane to move forward this quarter. One POC explicitly needs air-gapped capability but can be later. Revenue impact points to VPC-first.
Sasha: Proposed phased approach: Phase A: Control-plane-first (VPC) + migration playbook + minimal on-prem installer artifacts; Phase B: On-prem packaging with installer, dependency bundles, automation; Phase C: Air-gap hardened flow with signed bundles and import tooling. This gives wins quickly while de-risking airgap work.
Jun: From OKR perspective Phase A hits growth metrics (reduce deal cycle), Phase C maps to compliance OKRs. Recommend we set measurable targets per phase.
Taylor: Implementation notes for Phase A: we should publish a terraform module + helm chart for customer infra provisioning. Example snippet to standardize:
```
module "redwood_control_plane" {
  source = "git::https://repo.redwood.ai/infra/control-plane.git"
  region = var.region
  customer_id = var.customer_id
}
```
Also add feature flags for runtime fallback so private nodes can fall back to hosted if capacity issues detected.
Lina: Phase A security checklist (must pass before ship): 1) SSO SAML/OIDC end-to-end, 2) KMS integration validated (cloud KMS paths), 3) tenant isolation verified, 4) audit log export & retention doc, 5) compliance owner sign-off. Assign owner for each.
Omar: Add to launch pack: migration playbook (hosted -> VPC), pricing template for reserved capacity, and customer-facing FAQ about data residency. I'll draft comms and demo script.
Sasha: Draft launch criteria for Phase A (VPC-first): a) Control plane deployable into customer VPC with documented terraform/helm; b) SSO + KMS end-to-end tested; c) Basic SLA targets validated under load in two regions; d) Migration playbook and pricing template; e) Security/compliance sign-off.
Jun: Rough sprint plan: Installer-compat spike (2 weeks), control-plane terraform modules (3 weeks), SSO/KMS e2e tests (2 weeks), docs + playbook (1 week). We'll iterate in parallel.
Taylor: Ops/Runtime: implement a feature-flagged routing policy for model fallback and a per-tenant circuit breaker. That reduces blast radius during early customer rollouts.
Lina: I'll own the compliance checklist and provide a gating rubric for sign-off. If any customer requires HSM at launch, we should flag that separately (likely Phase B/C).
Omar: I'll notify the three active prospects and recommend Phase A as the fastest path. Will ask them to share specific regulatory constraints so we can triage.
Sasha: Action items: JUN - run installer compatibility spike and ship milestone timeline; TAYLOR - build terraform module + fallback plan; LINA - compliance checklist + owner assignments; OMAR - customer comms + pricing. I'll collate and run a 30-min sync Wed.
deploy-bot: Epic created "private/q3-controlplane-phased" (#4342).
Sasha: thanks — drop any blockers here. If anyone feels strongly we must do air-gap first, state it with customer examples and estimated revenue impact.
